title: Swap hand-rolled argv parsing for getopt_long
summary: Replace a strcmp loop over argv with getopt_long and a struct option table.

turns.user: i'm walking argv with strcmp and it crashes if -o is the last arg. also want -vo out.txt to work

assistant.body: Great catch. When -o comes last, argv[++i] is argv[argc], which is NULL, and run falls over on it. Let's drop the hand-rolled strcmp chain and let getopt_long do the parsing. Short options go in the "vo:" string and long ones in a struct option table, where the colon marks an option that takes an argument. Bundled flags like -vo out.txt and the --output=out.txt form both work, and a missing argument comes back as '?'. Note: getopt_long is not POSIX, but both glibc and the macOS libc ship it.

turns.user: want more detail with -v twice. like -vv

assistant.body: The trick is to count the flag instead of setting it. For -vv, getopt_long hands back 'v' twice, so verbose ends up at 2.
